extracted.intended_audience: readers interested in fashion industry, brand reputation, and crisis PR (general public and PR professionals)
extracted.subtask_short: crisis PR timeline for fashion brand
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological account of a fashion-brand public relations crisis, documenting actions, reactions, and outcomes for assessing crisis response and reputation impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid culturally insensitive advertising
rubrics_metrics.description: Promotional videos showed a Chinese model struggling to eat Italian dishes with chopsticks; commenters said it was patronizing, sexist, and even racist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example/anti-pattern: Using stereotypes or staged portrayals that mock local customs can provoke accusations of racism and sexism and spark immediate backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to local teams when expanding into new markets
rubrics_metrics.description: “Western brands that want to grow in China must listen to their local China teams,” advises Vogue editor in chief Angelica Cheung.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Heed local-market staff and cultural experts during campaign development to avoid tone-deaf messaging and to anticipate local reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue a timely, clear apology/statement to quell controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: A full statement is put out trying to quell the controversy, which says the show and the promotional videos had been meant as a tribute to China.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording used: framing the event as a 'tribute' and expressing 'love and passion' for China. Scoring note: speed and perceived sincerity matter; late or defensive statements are less effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use personal apologies and local language to demonstrate contrition
rubrics_metrics.description: Co-founders Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana issued a direct video apology, saying “dui bu qi” or “sorry” in Mandarin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: A direct, personal apology (especially delivered in the affected community’s language) can be a stronger signal of remorse than corporate statements, though timing and authenticity remain critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address claims of external sabotage (e.g., hacking) quickly and transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: Brand claims hacking as a defense for the Instagram messages; however, it’s too late and the event is canceled just hours before it is meant to kick off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Asserting that accounts were hacked must be accompanied by credible investigation details and evidence; otherwise such claims may be seen as excuses and fail to stem backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate and manage celebrity, model, and influencer boycotts
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrities, models, and influencers began swiftly boycotting the event (e.g., Zhang Ziyi said she would not attend or wear the brand again).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Influencer and celebrity dissociation can rapidly escalate reputational damage; PR response plans should consider outreach, mitigation, or contingency plans when public figures withdraw support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to cancel or postpone events if backlash escalates
rubrics_metrics.description: The event was canceled hours before it was meant to kick off amid the controversy and boycotts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Cancelling may be necessary to limit immediate harm, but it also signals severity of the crisis and has commercial/relationship consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for retail and e-commerce delisting as a likely repercussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Products were scrubbed from major Chinese e-commerce sites (Alibaba, JD, Secoo, Netease), and retailers like Yoox Net-a-porter and Luisa Via Roma removed the brand from their Chinese arms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Rapid platform and retail delisting is a common commercial fallout; brands should anticipate supply-chain and distribution impacts and have recovery/partner-reengagement plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Take security precautions at physical stores during heightened backlash
rubrics_metrics.description: Fearing backlash, guards were stationed at stores across China (seen at stores in Beijing and Shanghai).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Physical security measures may be necessary to protect staff and property during intense public anger, but they also publicly signal the seriousness of the backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expect global fallout and consider long-term strategic options
rubrics_metrics.description: Fallout went global with additional retailers removing the brand; commentators speculated about possible outcomes (a sale, a solo Dolce without Gabbana, or whether Chinese consumers will forgive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: Crises can have long-term brand consequences; organizations should evaluate strategic options (restructuring, leadership changes, brand rehabilitation) and not assume quick forgiveness from consumers.
